Implement a standalone ProductCatalogue for registering products and retrieving
their names and prices.

A newly created catalogue contains no products. product_count() returns the
number of distinct product identifiers currently registered.

register_product(sku, name, price) registers a product under the supplied sku.
product_name(sku) returns that product's registered name.
product_price(sku) returns that product's registered price.

Registering an already registered sku replaces that product's name and price
without increasing the product count. It must not change other registered
products.

Looking up the name or price of an unknown sku raises KeyError and leaves the
catalogue unchanged.

Reading a product's name, price or the product count does not change the
catalogue. Separate ProductCatalogue instances hold independent state.

For this behavior, valid skus and names are non-empty strings and valid prices
are non-negative integers representing minor currency units. Zero is a valid
price. Other input types or values are outside the specified input domain;
do not invent validation or exception requirements for them.

For example, registering ("bread", "Bread", 300) and ("milk", "Milk", 200)
produces a product count of 2. Looking up bread returns name "Bread" and price
300; looking up milk returns name "Milk" and price 200. Registering
("bread", "Wholemeal bread", 350) afterward keeps the count at 2, updates
bread's name and price, and leaves milk unchanged.

The catalogue is standalone, dependency-free and in memory. It does not call
a basket, order register, network service, filesystem storage or database.
